ABSTRACT Background The anti‐inflammatory cytokine interleukin‐4 (IL4) has been recognised as a protective factor in various cardiovascular events, yet its prognostic value in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH) remains unclear. The study aimed to measure the levels of plasma IL4 in patients with PH and to explore their potential association with disease risk and outcomes. Methods In this observational study, we analysed the levels of plasma IL4 in 766 PH patients and 191 healthy controls in Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital from October 2009 to January 2024. To establish the correlations between plasma IL4 levels and the risk and outcomes of PH, all patients were followed up from June 2013 to June 2024. The Spearman correlation test was employed to evaluate the relationships between IL4 and right heart catheterisation parameters among patients with PH. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated to evaluate the diagnostic performance of IL4 for PH. The Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan–Meier survival curves were used to assess the prognostic value of IL4 levels. Logistic regression analysis was performed to predict PH incidence. A nomogram was constructed to predict mortality, and its clinical utility was validated using decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Plasma IL4 levels were significantly decreased in patients with PH compared with controls ( p < 0.001), as well as in different PH groups ( p < 0.05 for all). The logistic regression analyses indicated that the lower IL4 levels were associated with the high risk of PH (OR = 0.79, 95% CI: 0.716–0.872; p < 0.001). IL4 levels correlated inversely with NT‐proBNP ( r = −0.10, p < 0.05) and mPAP ( r = −0.01, p < 0.05), and positively with CI ( r = 0.12, p < 0.05) and PaSaO2 ( r = 0.11, p < 0.05), indicating an association with disease severity. Kaplan–Meier analysis revealed that patients with IL4 ≥ 2.8774 pg/mL had a 3‐year cumulative survival rate of 91.28%, compared with 82.83% for those with IL4 < 2.8774 pg/mL (log–rank p = 0.007). Cox regression confirmed IL4 as an independent predictor of survival (HR = 0.810, 95% CI: 0.660–0.993; p = 0.043). A diagnostic model combining IL4, 6MWD and NT‐proBNP demonstrated good prognostic value (AUC = 0.692, p < 0.0001). extracted_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated plasma Interleukin-4 (IL4) levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH) and healthy controls, finding significantly decreased IL4 levels in PH patients. Lower plasma IL4 was associated with higher PH risk, greater disease severity, increased clinical worsening, and poorer survival rates, indicating its potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for PH.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating endogenous biomarker levels in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study; no therapeutic interventions or dose comparisons were performed. Endogenous plasma IL4 levels were measured by flow cytometry in 766 PH patients and 191 healthy controls.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly decreased in PH patients (p < 0.001) compared to controls (median 2.0 pg/mL vs 2.8 pg/mL), and also lower across various PH subtypes (G1, G2, G4 PH, IPAH, CHD, p < 0.05 for all). Lower IL4 levels were associated with a higher risk of PH (OR = 0.79, 95% CI: 0.716–0.872; p < 0.001). IL4 correlated inversely with NT-proBNP (r = −0.10, p < 0.05) and mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP, r = −0.01, p < 0.05), and positively with cardiac index (CI, r = 0.12, p < 0.05) and arterial oxygen saturation (PaSaO2, r = 0.11, p < 0.05). Patients with IL4 < 2.8774 pg/mL showed a significantly lower 3-year cumulative survival rate (82.83%) compared to those with IL4 ≥ 2.8774 pg/mL (91.28%, log-rank p = 0.007). IL4 was confirmed as an independent predictor of survival (HR = 0.810, 95% CI: 0.660–0.993; p = 0.043). The AUC for IL4 in PH diagnosis was 0.63 (p < 0.0001), and a model combining IL4, 6MWD, and NT-proBNP had an AUC of 0.692 (p < 0.0001) for prognostic value.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An anti-inflammatory Th2 cytokine involved in PH development, exhibiting a dual role by promoting vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation and remodeling while also having protective anti-inflammatory effects via M2 macrophages. It plays a role in the initial response to injury and regulation of pulmonary vascular remodeling.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, disease severity across various subtypes (G1, G2, G4 PH, IPAH, CHD), clinical outcomes, disease progression, and patient survival.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for PH, reflecting overall disease burden and severity. Lower IL4 levels are associated with increased PH risk, greater disease severity (linked to adverse hemodynamic parameters), clinical deterioration, and significantly poorer survival rates, allowing for patient stratification into risk groups.
